Loopar ships a CLI that drives the core through a **project-local PM2 daemon**. Run commands with `yarn <command>` from the project root.

> **Mode is global.** Development (Vite + HMR) or production (prebuilt bundle) applies to the whole core — toggle it with `m` in the TUI or `yarn prod`. It is not a per-tenant or per-command setting.

---

## Lifecycle

```bash
yarn start               # open the TUI (and start the core if it is down)
yarn serve               # headless boot in the mode config/core.json says (servers, CI)
yarn prod                # switch the core to production (needs a build) and boot
yarn stop                # stop the core (or a named process: yarn stop build-watch)
yarn restart             # restart the core (re-reads config/core.json)
yarn delete [proc]       # remove the core (or a process) from the PM2 registry
yarn kill                # kill every process AND the daemon (clean slate)
```

## Tenants

```bash
yarn tenant list         # every tenant and its status
yarn tenant on  my-site  # turn a tenant on
yarn tenant off my-site  # turn it off (it serves a "suspended" page; data is kept)
```

## Inspection

```bash
yarn tui                 # same as yarn start
yarn logs                # tail every process
yarn logs loopar-core    # tail one process
```

## Operations

```bash
yarn startup                     # reboot-safe boot hook (run once on a server)
yarn backup ...                  # tenant backups — see the Backups page
yarn admin-reset <site> [email]  # create the Administrator or give it a temporary password
yarn mfa-reset <site> <user>     # turn 2FA off for a user who lost their phone and codes
yarn migrate                     # one-shot: legacy sites/<t>/.env → config.json
```

## Build

```bash
yarn build               # full production build (versioned release, atomic swap)
yarn watch               # background builder → build/staging (stop: yarn stop build-watch)
yarn activate            # promote build/staging to a new live release (fast deploy)
```

## Tests

```bash
yarn test                # unit + integration
yarn test:unit           # pure modules only
```

Every command also works as `node bin/cli/index.js <command>`; `node bin/cli/index.js help` lists them.
"}},{"node":"cli-tui","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"TUI","key":"cli-tui","id":"cli-tui","name":"cli-tui","value":"## The TUI

`yarn start` opens a full tenant manager in the terminal (mouse supported):

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `↑ ↓` / `j k` | Select a tenant |
| `o` | Open the tenant in the browser (install link if it isn't installed yet) |
| `s` / `t` / `r` | Turn on / turn off / restart |
| `n` | New tenant |
| `l` | Logs of the selected tenant · `L` merged logs of every process |
| `m` | Switch the core between development and production |
| `c` | Start the core when it is down (or restart it) |
| `B` | Backups of the selected tenant |
| `T` | Tests tab |
| `e` / `d` | Reset / destroy a tenant (asks you to type its name) |
| `q` | Quit |

> Always use the `yarn` commands instead of a global `pm2` — they target the project's own daemon.


### Tabs

| Tab | Open with | What it does |
|-----|-----------|--------------|
| Tenants | (default) | The list above, with the core's state in the header |
| Logs | `l` / `L` | Realtime logs of a tenant or of every process; arrows scroll, `f` follows again, `a` toggles the scope |
| Backups | `B` | Backups of the selected tenant: `n` now, `r` restore, `d` delete |
| Tests | `T` | Run the test suite: `a` all, `u` unit, `i` integration, `f` failed, `x` stop |
